subject: POC: Prompt/eval dataset collection & evaluation plan - Acme Health
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Miller <jordan.miller@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@acmehealth.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Jul 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: POC follow-up: prompt set + eval dataset (next steps)

Hi Jordan / Priya —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps to get the POC rolling:

1) Goal & success criteria
- Primary: reliably match current triage accuracy (>92% F1 on labeled sample) while reducing average inference latency to <200ms per request for our "concise" prompt type.
- Secondary: reduce per-1k token cost by at least 30% vs current hosted baseline.

2) Evaluation plan
- You provide: ~500 representative prompts (mix of short triage, long context, and follow-up clarification), plus a labeled evaluation set (~200 examples) and a sampling of logs (redacted) showing typical user flows.
- We'll: run A/B tests across two model variants (open-llama-13B-qlora, redwood-opt-6B-quant) with identical prompt templates; compute accuracy, latency, and token-cost metrics; and return a performance dashboard.

3) Timeline & ownership
- T+0 (this week): Customer shares prompt CSV + redacted logs. Marissa will validate and confirm formatting.
- T+3 business days: Redwood spins up POC runs and shares preliminary results.
- T+10 business days: Final POC report and recommendation.

4) Data transfer and security
- Please upload prompts/logs to the shared Google Drive folder (link below) or provide an S3 pre-signed URL. We only need redacted logs; do not include PHI. Our Private POC environment will be used and logs will be deleted after the POC unless you opt-in for retention.

Attachments: I've attached a CSV template (acme_prompt_sample.csv) and our standard POC evaluation plan (rdw_poc_eval_plan.docx).

Next steps: Jordan — can you upload the prompt CSV and one week of redacted logs to the Drive by end of day Wednesday? If S3 is easier, send a pre-signed link.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0142

Appreciate the clear plan. We're aligned on the success criteria. We'll do the following:
- Priya will export ~600 prompts that cover the triage + clarification flows and a labeled set of ~220 items.
- We'll redact user identifiers and PHI; logs will be zipped (acme_logs_redacted.zip).
- We'll upload everything to the Drive folder you linked by COB Wednesday (14 Jul).

One question: for the labeled eval set, do you prefer a CSV with columns (prompt, expected_label, notes) or a JSONL with schema? We can do either.

CSV with columns (prompt, expected_label, notes) is perfect — thanks. We'll accept JSONL too but CSV is easiest. I've looped in Aditya (infra) to confirm compute profile and any sampling we should do on the logs.

Quick internal note and action items:

- Plan: We'll run the labeled eval set across two configurations:
  1) redwood-opt-6B-quant (low-cost baseline): batch size 8, quantized FP16 path
  2) open-llama-13B-qlora (higher accuracy): batch size 4, KV caching enabled
- Metrics: accuracy/F1, 95th pct latency, median latency, cost-per-1k tokens.
- Need from customer: confirmation of sample sequence length distribution (mean tokens) so we can pick sequence truncation and kernel selection.

Action items:
- Marissa: confirm when files are uploaded and share Drive/S3 link.
- Neha: prepare the evaluation dashboard template and a short README for interpreting results.

I'll start provisioning capacity now so we have runs queued as soon as data arrives.
